What is Communication?

What communication is, its process, types and why it matters in nursing.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define communication and list its elements
  • Describe the communication process
  • Explain why communication matters in nursing

In simple words

Communication is the exchange of information, ideas and feelings between people. It can be through words (verbal) or without words (non-verbal).

Good communication builds trust, helps assessment, and makes care safer. Poor communication causes errors, misunderstanding and complaints.

Elements of communication

Element Meaning Example
Sender The person who sends the message The nurse
Message The information sent “Take this medicine after food”
Channel The way it is sent Speaking, writing, phone
Receiver The person who gets it The patient
Feedback The receiver’s response The patient nods or asks a question
Barrier Anything that blocks understanding Noise, language difference

Types of communication

  • Verbal — spoken or written words.
  • Non-verbal — body language, facial expression, touch, eye contact, posture.
  • Formal — official records, reports, handover.
  • Informal — casual talk with patients and colleagues.

Most meaning comes from non-verbal cues — tone, expression and gestures often matter more than words.

🔴 Definition examiners use

Communication is the exchange of information, ideas and feelings between people through a sender, message, channel, receiver and feedback.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Handover — give clear, complete information to the next shift.
  • Patient teaching — explain procedures and medicines in plain language.
  • Consent — make sure the patient understands before agreeing.
  • Emotional support — listen and respond to feelings, not just facts.
  • Documentation — write clearly so the next person understands.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Communication is the exchange of information, ideas and feelings between people.
  2. Elements: sender, message, channel, receiver, feedback.
  3. Barriers include noise, language difference and poor listening.
  4. Types: verbal, non-verbal, formal and informal.
  5. Non-verbal cues (tone, expression, gesture) carry much of the meaning.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Formal communication includes records, reports and handover.
  2. Verbal communication is spoken or written words.
  3. Feedback confirms the message was understood.

📌 Memory trick

Communication elements: “S-M-C-R-F” — Sender, Message, Channel, Receiver, Feedback. Say “smurf”.

60-second revision

  • Communication = exchange of information, ideas, feelings.
  • Elements: sender → message → channel → receiver → feedback.
  • Types: verbal, non-verbal, formal, informal.
  • Barriers: noise, language, poor listening.
  • Non-verbal carries much of the meaning.

Test yourself

Communication is the exchange of:

Answer: B. Communication exchanges information, ideas and feelings, not only words.

Which is NOT an element of communication?

Answer: D. Diagnosis is a medical act, not a communication element.

Non-verbal communication includes:

Answer: C. Non-verbal communication uses body language, expression, touch and eye contact.

Feedback in communication means:

Answer: B. Feedback is the receiver's response, showing whether the message was understood.

Formal communication in nursing includes:

Answer: B. Handover and patient records are formal communication.
